messages.subject: Re: Global variables in nimbleFunction
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

No, there isn't a system for global variables.  Your approach is very reasonable.

Another way to do it would be to have MEANINGOFLIFE passed as an argument to setup code.  If it is then used in run code, the compiler will make it be member data in the under-the-hood C++ class.  A variant on this idea would be to create a nimbleFunction with setup code whose only purpose really is to hold the MEANINGOFLIFE value.  An object of this nimbleFunction could then be passed to setup code of other nimbleFunctions, and they will all access the same object, hence the same single MEANINGOFLIFE value.  However, these approaches will not work if the nimbleFunctions you are writing are to be used in models (as user-defined distributions or model functions), because those can't have setup code.

After thinking through these options, your solution seems perhaps easiest of all.

-Perry

On Wed, Jan 9, 2019 at 2:34 AM 'Joseph Chipperfield' via nimble-users <nimble...@googlegroups.com> wrote:

> Happy New Year everyone!
>
> I was just wondering if there is a simple way to define and use global constants that can be used in compiled user-defined nimbleFunctions.  For example, the following wouldn't work:
>
> # Define a global constant
> MEANINGOFLIFE <- 42
>
> # Define a user-defined function
> myFunctionA <- nimbleFunction(
>     run = function(
>         # Parameter list here...
>     ) {
>         # Some code that uses MEANINGOFLIFE
>     }
> )
>
> because under compilation the MEANINGOFLIFE is not defined and resolved (as it exists in an R environment only).
>
> I've instead been doing the following:
>
> # Define a function that does nothing except return the global constant
> meaningOfLife <- nimbleFunction(
>     run = function(
>         # No parameters
>     ) {
>         returnType(integer(0))
>         return(42)
>     }
> )
>
> # Define a user-defined function
> myFunctionA <- nimbleFunction(
>     run = function(
>          # Parameter list here...
>     ) {
>          # Some code that calls the global constant function
>          meaningOfLife()
>     }
> )
>
> But this seems a bit clunky and maybe I'm missing an obvious easier way.
>
> Thanks for any help you can give.
>
> Joe

My understanding is that it should be possible with NIMBLE to do this without recompiling as long as they are entered as data rather than constants. However, every example I can find that uses setdata or resetdata has a compilation step prior to to rerunning with runMCMC. Is there a way to do this?

messages.subject: Re: Running compiled NIMBLE moel with new data
messages.subject_clean: Running compiled NIMBLE moel with new data
messages.body_plain:
We have seen in the past some confusion about setData and resetData.  These are primarily intended for uncompiled models.  They do two things: They say which variables should be flagged as data, and they set the values of those variables.  The data flags are used, for example, in deciding what should be sampled in an MCMC.  With a compiled model, setData will modify the data values, but it will not change which variables are flagged as data.  And in a typical workflow, the compiled model is made after an MCMC configuration is made, hence after the data flags have been used.

What you want to do is much simpler.  You can always access and modify model variables in the compiled model like a typical R object.  If cModel is a compiled model, you can say

cModel$my_data <- some_new_values

etc.

The limitation on re-using a compiled model is that the sizes of all variables can't change.  The model must really be identical.  If that is not the case, it may be possible to create a largest-needed model and then make multiple MCMCs for different subsets of it.

-Perry

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Perry for once again straightening out my confusion. Much appreciated. I am however further confused. The below code creates two compiled versions of the code: CHunting and CompiledHuntMCMC.
The former has the CHunting$K that I want change for each implementation of the analysis with a new data (which always have the same dimension), but it won't run, giving the error message:
runMCMC(CHunting)
Error in nf_getGeneratorFunction(mcmc) : invalid nimbleFunction argument

The latter runs fine, but it contains no CompiledHuntMCMC$K that I can change.

Any ideas of where I'm veering off the track?

Code:
require("nimble")

NegBinHuntCode<- nimbleCode({

  for (r in 1:Reports){

    # Number of killed animals in report r is negative binomial distributed,
    # but defined from the mean (m[KretsNr[r]]*A[r]) and coefficient of variation (c[Lan[r]]) of the gamma distribution of the equivalent gamma-poisson mixture
    K[r] ~ dnegbin(1/(1+m[KretsNrSeqID[r]]*A[r]*c[LanSeqID[r]]^2),c[LanSeqID[r]]^-2)
  }

  for(ik in 1:length(KretsarSeqID)){

    m[ik] <- exp(logL[KretsListLanSeqID[ik]]+logK[ik]) #m[Kretsar[ik]] is the mean killing rate per area in circuit Kretsar[ik]

    logK[ik] ~ dnorm(0,kretsprec[KretsListLanSeqID[ik]]) # logK[Kretsar[ik]] is the circuit random effect of circuit Kretsar[ik]

    SamplePoiss[ik] ~ dpois(m[ik]*UnreportedAperkretsSeqID[ik]) #  samples how much was killed on the unreported area of circuit Kretsar[ik], assuming a poinsson process

  }
  for (il in 1:length(LansSeqID)){
    logL[il] ~ dnorm(logS,lansprec) # logL[Lans[il]] is the county level random effect of county L
    kretsprec[il] ~ dgamma(kretsprecalpha,kretsprecalpha/kretsprecmean) # kretsprec[Lans[il]]  is the precission parameter for the hierarchical distribution of circuit effects with county Lans[il]

    c[il] <- exp(logcmean+logckrets[il]) # c[Lans[il]] is the coefficient of variation as above
    logckrets[il] ~ dnorm(0,logcprec) # county level effect for c

  }
  logS ~ dnorm(0,.001)
  logcmean ~ dnorm(0,.01)
  logcprec ~ dgamma(.01,.01)
  kretsprecalpha ~ dgamma(.01,.01)
  kretsprecmean  ~ dgamma(.01,.01)
  lansprec ~ dgamma(.01,.01)

})

Constants <- list(A=A,Reports=Reports,KretsNrSeqID=KretsNrSeqID,Lan=Lan,LansSeqID=LansSeqID,LanSeqID=LanSeqID,KretsarSeqID=KretsarSeqID,KretsListLanSeqID=KretsListLanSeqID,UnreportedAperkretsSeqID=UnreportedAperkretsSeqID)
Data <- list(K=K)
Inits <- list(c=rep(1,length(LansSeqID)),logL=rep(-7,length(LansSeqID)),logK=rep(0,length(KretsarSeqID)),logcmean=0,logckrets=rep(0,length(LansSeqID)),kretsprec=rep(1,length(LansSeqID)),logS=-7,logcprec=1,kretsprecalpha=1,kretsprecmean=1,lansprec=1)

Hunting <- nimbleModel(code = NegBinHuntCode, name = "hunt", constants = Constants,
                       data = Data, inits = Inits)
Hunting$getNodeNames()

CHunting <- compileNimble(Hunting)

HuntConf <- configureMCMC(Hunting, print = TRUE)
HuntConf$addMonitors(c("logS", "logcmean","logcprec","kretsprecalpha","kretsprecmean","lansprec","logckrets","c","kretsprec","logL","SamplePoiss","logK","m"))

HuntMCMC <- buildMCMC(HuntConf)

niter=1000
CompiledHuntMCMC <- compileNimble(HuntMCMC, project = Hunting)
samples <- runMCMC(CompiledHuntMCMC, niter = niter)

Thanks for the clear example.

CHunting is a compiled model.

CompiledHuntingMCMC is a compiled MCMC algorithm that uses CHunting.

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm running a bit of a complex model that requires model fitting, model predicting, a nimbleFunction(), and then another model fitting step all within one iteration.  I'm running into an issue where I'm trying to use a "posterior_predictive" node as the input to a nimbleFunction().  No matter what I've tried (defining the node first as different types or within the nimbleFunction), I can't seem to get it to work.  I receive the following error message:

> modelModel <- nimbleModel(code = modelCode, constants = modelConsts, data = modelData, inits = list(beta0 = 0, beta1 = 0))
defining model...
Error in genVarInfo3() :
  Dimension of PM is 1, which does not match its usage in 'y_matrix <- Counting2(PM)'.

I'm not clear why it thinks the dimension is 1 when it should see it as "N_20" or 240.

Please see the attached R file.  Although the data set is random, the "Counting2" nimbleFunction is the exact function I'm using.  What is strange is that the nimbleFunction() I've created, Counting2, will work outside of the nimbleCode(), and I have an example of this in the last few lines of the attached R file.

I am wondering if what I'm trying to do is possible by NIMBLE or if I'm just doing something wrong.  I don't see anything in the manual that says you can't do this, but I also don't see anything that says I can.

Thanks so much for your time.

Best,

Matthew

messages.body_plain:
Hi Matthew,

Thanks for the query and code.

I think there is some confusion about type declarations and differences between R and nimble in numeric(), along with some need for clarification on how things work.

The type declaration I think you want is:
run = function(PM_resp = double(1))

That says that PM_resp is a 1-dimensional double (i.e. a double vector).

A line like:
y1_1 <- numeric(N_20)
should be
y1_1 <- numeric(length = N_20)
(but may not be necessary: see below)

You'll need to pass OF into the function for it to work compiled.  Uncompiled, I guess it is being found by scoping.

You can vectorize such as:
size_2020_is_1 <- size_2020 == 1
OF_is_1 <- OF == 1
PM_resp_is_1 <- PM_resp == 1
y1_1 <- sum(size_2020_is_1 & OF_is_1 & PM_resp_is1)

Please note that after you create y1_1 as a vector, you can't then use it as a scalar (but in my example, you don't need the vector version).  nimbleFunctions need to behave as if variables are statically typed to compile correctly.

You want "returnType(double(1))".  The "8" in your code would be number of dimensions, which isn't what you want and we only support 4 (soon to be 5 by popular demand).

In modelCode, indices must always be explicit.  For example, you want:
y_matrix[1:N_20] <- Counting2(PM[1:N_20])

The model declaration language does not support multiple declarations for the same node.  It is a declarative language.

I recommend the NimbleUserManual.pdf at R-nimble.org to you.

-Perry
